newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pac Dunlop sells Telectronics unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pac Dunlop sells Telectronics unit.

text.p: Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Wednesday it had sold its pacemaker manufacturer, Telectronics, for A$170 million.

Pacific Dunlop said the buyer was St Jude Medical Inc. The agreement, subject to U.S. government review, includes an earnout provision tied to future sales which could result in additional payments of up to US$25 million by 2002.
Responsibility for Telectronics products made prior to the sale has not been assumed by St Jude, Pacific Dunlop said.
St Jude develops and manufactures medical devices for the global cardiovascular market.
Pac Dunlop said the Accufix Research Institute would remain in the Pac Dunlop group with Telectronics having previously announced a provision of A$85 million for the Institute's costs.
The Institute was established after the recall of Accufix pacemaker leads, the source of much legal action against the company.

On September 13, PacDun said it had recorded an abnormal loss of A$340 million in respect of Telectronics in the year to June 30, 1996 and had provided A$91 million in the 1995/96 results for the expected loss on Telectronics.
Pacific Dunlop shares closed two cents lower at A$2.78 on turnover of 1.23 million shares.
